clue.text: Hiding place many yearn to find

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to yearn is to ache for something

explanation.surface: A treasure-hunter's dream: the secret spot everyone longs to discover.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a concealed store, a stash kept out of sight.

clue.text: Secures rent for one of a group of shops

definitions.text: one of a group of shops

parts.note: to secure with fetters is to chain, so secures gives chains
rent as a past tense of rend means torn, here tore

explanation.surface: A landlord locks up and collects rent for one of several retail units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord, but it is the past of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A multiple retailer has many branches under one owner, each outlet belonging to the network.

clue.text: Two birds seen in early part of the day

parts.note: a cock is a male fowl
a crow is a black bird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a pair of birds at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is marked by the rooster's call, so the term names daybreak.

clue.text: Quits faulty planes

explanation.surface: Someone gives up because the aircraft are defective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quits' is the adjective, as in being quits, and the phrase also means smoothing out, planing down, uneven or faulty surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be quits is to settle level, making things square; and a carpenter planes faulty bumps flat, levelling them.

clue.text: Fly doctors to south American capital

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, army doctors
Quito is the capital of Ecuador, in South America

explanation.surface: Medics take a flight down to an Andean capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb about travelling, but it is the insect, which carries malaria in such places.
explanation.definitionFit: The mosquito is a small two-winged insect, a true dipteran.

clue.text: Rugs obtained by mother on the back street

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: on the back says the abbreviation for street is turned backwards

explanation.surface: Floor coverings that Mum picks up on a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the back' reads as part of 'back street', but it is the reversal signal working on the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Small floor coverings, mats and rugs are much the same thing.

clue.text: What one may give a quid for — drink for enough people

parts.words: What one may give a quid for
parts.note: quid pro quo: the quid is given for the quo, the Latin for something in return
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone pays a pound for a drink, plus a round for the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quid' looks like slang for a pound, but it is the Latin of quid pro quo, something for something.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum number of members needed for a meeting to proceed is called this.

clue.text: This led Mrs Gandhi to be queen in her own country

indicators.note: in says the letter for queen sits inside the name of the country

parts.note: Mrs Gandhi's own country is India
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The prime minister was destined to become a queen in her homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian prime minister Mrs Gandhi had that first name.

clue.text: Unfasten the duck cage

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O
a pen is an enclosure, a cage

explanation.surface: Someone lets a duck out of its cage.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a lock or catch is to make it no longer shut.

clue.text: Vouch for the account, many tried falsely!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, standing for many

indicators.note: falsely says the letters of tried are not set out truthfully but rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone backs up a bookkeeping record that has been fiddled many times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsely' rearranges the word tried into REDIT; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit is to give official recognition or endorsement, to certify as genuine.

clue.text: It may turn tail and still be aggressive

definitions.text: It may turn tail and still be aggressive

parts.words: It may turn tail and still be aggressive
parts.note: turning tail usually means retreating, but this arachnid curls its stinging tail forward over its back to attack

explanation.surface: A creature that seems to flee yet remains on the attack.
explanation.definitionFit: This arachnid arches its venomous tail over its body when it strikes.

clue.text: Pieces played in correct, but not right, order

indicators.note: order says the remaining letters are put in a new sequence
but not says a letter is dropped from the fodder

explanation.surface: Music performed in the proper sequence, though not quite properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes one R from IN CORRECT, and 'order' rearranges what is left, INCOECT plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Concertos are musical works, compositions for soloist and orchestra.

clue.text: Despoiled icon is restored to a foreign city

indicators.note: despoiled says the letters of the words are ransacked and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A plundered religious picture is returned to a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despoiled' rearranges ICON IS into NICOSI before the A; 'restored to' is a link, though it reads like a second shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital of Cyprus, a city overseas from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Only men go in at such a meeting

indicators.note: go in says the pieces enter the word at

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gathering admits males alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only' as BUT is a crossword staple ('but a moment'); 'such a' is a link, and an abutment is where a bridge meets its support.
explanation.definitionFit: A point where two things touch or join, as a bridge meets its support.

clue.text: Definitely not many bones broken

indicators.note: broken says the letters of many bones are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone insists, in fact, that hardly any bones were fractured.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic phrase of denial, meaning not at all or in no way.

clue.text: Big build-up in new York, for example

definitions.text: Big build-up in new York, for example

parts.words: Big build-up in new York, for example
parts.note: reads like a lot of hype in New York, but means a tall building put up there

explanation.surface: Lots of hype in the Big Apple.
explanation.definitionFit: A very tall building, of the kind Manhattan is famous for.

clue.text: Two, Timothy and Helen, in arrangement of aria

indicators.note: in arrangement of says the letters of the names are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Two singers, Timothy and Helen, perform a musical arrangement of an aria together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' looks like a musical arrangement, fitting the aria, but it is the anagram signal working on TWO TIMOTHY HELEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the English title of Canio's famous lament in Leoncavallo's opera Pagliacci, Vesti la giubba.

clue.text: Layman has little chance of success

explanation.surface: A non-expert is unlikely to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A layman stands beyond a profession's circle; and a long shot in a race is a horse unlikely to win.

clue.text: Those trying for a licence or degree?

definitions.text: Those trying for a licence or degree?

parts.words: Those trying for a licence or degree?
parts.note: learner drivers try for a licence, and students study for a degree

explanation.surface: Applicants for a driving permit or a university qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: People studying a skill are students; L-plate drivers are called this.

clue.text: A run to clinch the match?

definitions.text: A run to clinch the match?

parts.words: A run to clinch the match?
parts.note: sounds like a sporting run that wins a game, but means running away to secure a marriage, a match of lovers

explanation.surface: A batsman's dash to seal victory in a cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: Running off secretly to marry is this; match here means a marriage.

clue.text: From Baltimore go north for this state

indicators.note: From says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Directions from Baltimore heading north toward an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside Baltimore and spans 'go'; N for north completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pacific Northwest US state, one of the fifty.

clue.text: Set me up to supervise relief work

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word me is read upwards, turning it round

parts.note: taken as written
to boss is to supervise

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be put in charge of disaster aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief work' looks like aid for victims, but means raised decoration. 'up' turns ME into EM; 'Set' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a design so it stands out from a surface is to create raised decoration.

clue.text: He takes risks when others take cover

definitions.text: He takes risks when others take cover

parts.words: He takes risks when others take cover
parts.note: reads like a hero braving danger while others hide, but describes an underwriter who accepts risks when clients buy insurance cover

explanation.surface: A brave soul who stays exposed while everyone else shelters.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwriter accepts the financial risk of a policy that clients buy for protection.

clue.text: Run around a little, it won't do much harm

indicators.note: around says the word for run goes round the outside of the other piece

parts.note: to run away is to flee
a little means a bit

explanation.surface: Advice to dash about a bit, since a little exercise never hurt anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's nip is a trivial irritation, a minor annoyance rather than an injury.

clue.text: Business settled

explanation.surface: A company has been established.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is a business; and something fixed and stable is settled.

clue.text: Some rules Pythagoras had to observe

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A geometry student had to follow certain of Pythagoras's rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'had to observe' does not substitute for the answer; 'had to' is the link and 'observe' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of is to observe, a literary synonym for see.

clue.text: Dude pals prepare to ride on the ranch

indicators.note: on the ranch is a loose signal that the letters of dude pals are rounded up and mixed like cattle

explanation.surface: City visitors at a dude ranch get ready to go riding with their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the ranch' rearranges DUDE PALS; a dude is a city tourist on a Western holiday ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a horse ready for riding means fastening its seat on, the usual cowboy phrase for mounting up.

clue.text: Short skirts strain the cloth

parts.note: minis are miniskirts
to strain is to try hard

explanation.surface: Tight little skirts put pressure on the fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' looks like fabric, but it is the idiom for clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is an idiom for the clergy, the body of clerical ministers.

clue.text: It goes straight up in flight

definitions.text: It goes straight up in flight

parts.words: It goes straight up in flight
parts.note: suggests a rocket or bird soaring vertically, but a flight here is a staircase, whose vertical board between treads goes straight up

explanation.surface: Something shoots vertically upward while airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: In a flight of stairs, the vertical panel between steps is so named.
